sources.entry: Tameo - Privacy-first clipboard manager with history search, on-device image OCR, and snippets.

summary.one_liner: Tameo is a privacy-first, menu-bar clipboard manager for macOS 14+ (Apple Silicon and Intel) with full-text history search, on-device image OCR, encrypted history, and snippets.
summary.what_it_does: Tameo runs in the macOS menu bar and records copied items into a local history: plain text, rich text (RTF/RTFD), PDF, images, file paths, URLs, and color codes. A global hotkey (default ⌘⇧V) opens a floating palette at the cursor, where pressing 1–0 pastes an item into the frontmost app. Typing filters history, including Japanese IME input with full/half-width and hiragana/katakana folding. Items can be pinned, deleted, and filtered by type. On-device Vision OCR makes text inside copied images searchable and pasteable. Snippets are organized in folders, callable from the same palette (default ⌘⇧B), and can be imported from or exported to Clipy. The README states that concealed password-manager items, excluded apps, and disabled types are filtered before any content is read, and that history is always AES-GCM encrypted with the key in the Keychain.
use_cases: find text inside a screenshot I copied
store reusable snippets and canned replies
clipboard history without sending data to a server
notable: Filters pasteboard types, concealed items, and excluded apps before reading any content
History always encrypted at rest with AES-GCM, key in Keychain, no off switch
On-device OCR over copied images and screenshots, Vision framework
Japanese-first: kana and width variant folding in search, JIS layout support
Clean-room reimplementation inspired by Clipy with no code reuse
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later and Accessibility permission to paste into other apps
Building from source requires a full Xcode install
UI is in English only per the README, though the README itself includes Japanese text
